title: Private Deployments — Comprehensive Reference (VPC, On-Prem, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades & Customer Requirements)
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Introduction:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended reference architectures, deployment guides, on-prem packaging notes, day-2 operational runbooks, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended as a single entry point for Solutions Engineering, Customer SREs, the Eng Private Deployments team, and partner integrators.

Scope and Audience:
- Scope: VPC deployments (major cloud providers), air-gapped on-prem installs, day-2 operations, upgrade/rollback, and customer requirements.
- Audience: Solutions Engineering, Customer SREs, Eng Private Deployments team, Partner Integrators.

Executive Summary:
This reference provides: architecture diagrams described in text, minimum and recommended resource profiles, network and security requirements, packaging and install options (Helm/OCI bundle/offline installer), detailed day-2 runbooks (monitoring, backups, scaling), step-by-step upgrade and rollback procedures (canary and full rollbacks), and a customer requirements checklist with common pitfalls and mitigations.

1) Architecture Overview
Goals:
- Predictable tenant isolation when required (network & storage).
- Performance targets: platform availability 99.95%, p95 API TTFB < 120ms for small requests (aim for Dedicated parity).
- Secure defaults: least privilege, encryption in transit, customer-managed keys for sensitive data where requested.

Supported Topologies (high level):
- VPC Single-AZ: cost-sensitive, non-critical staging.
- VPC Multi-AZ: production (recommended).
- Hybrid: control plane in Redwood VPC, data plane in customer VPC.
- Fully On-Prem: air-gapped option with customer-managed control plane.

Core Components (textual diagram):
- control-plane: management API, rollout controller, license & telemetry (optional; can be deployed in customer VPC or Redwood-hosted).
- data-plane: inference runtime (GPU nodes), routing & autoscaler, KV cache layer.
- observability: metrics exporter (Prometheus), logs (Fluentd/Vector), traces (OTLP).
- data-storage: model registry and artifacts (S3/GCS for cloud or NFS/PVC for on-prem).

2) VPC Reference Architecture (recommended)
Network layout (recommended):
- Public subnets: external load balancers and NAT gateways.
- Private subnets: control plane, data plane, management services.
- Bastion hosts: emergency access only; restrict to customer IP ranges and MFA.
- Common ports to document with customers: 443/TCP (public API), 8443/TCP (internal control API with mTLS), 50051/TCP (runtime gRPC, internal), 9100/TCP (node exporters/metrics), 22/TCP (bastion, locked down).

Security controls and recommendations:
- Security groups aligned to least privilege; avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress for internal services.
- mTLS between control plane and data plane; mutual authentication using customer or Redwood-issued certs depending on deployment mode.
- KMS integration: recommend customer-managed keys for enterprises; Redwood-managed keys are available for lower friction pilots.

Compute and storage sizing (profiles):
- Small (POC): 1 inference replica, 2 vCPU control-plane, ~100 GiB PV for artifacts.
- Medium (pilot): 2-4 GPUs (A10G / T4), 4 control-plane replicas, ~500 GiB PVC or object store.
- Large (production): 8+ GPUs (A100/Tr4 class), autoscaling GPU pools, separate KV cache cluster, 2 TiB+ model store.

3) On-Prem Packaging & Air-Gapped Installs
Packaging options and recommended patterns:
- Helm chart + OCI image bundle (preferred for air-gapped customers).
- Offline tarball: release bundle containing container images (tar.gz), manifests, and a digest file for verification.
- Appliance (VM image) for customers without Kubernetes; supported as a special-case deployment.

Install preconditions (on-prem):
- Kubernetes 1.22+ with CSI and admission controllers enabled.
- Persistent storage supporting RWX if using a shared model store; otherwise per-node PVCs may be used.
- Node GPUs with supported drivers and CUDA runtime (see Driver Matrix in Appendix A).
- Internal registry (Harbor, Artifactory) for mirrored images in air-gapped environments.
- NTP/time sync configured across cluster.

Air-gapped install (high level steps):
1) Run preflight validation: ./preflight/check.sh --bundle rl-bundle-2026.tar.gz
2) Load images into local registry: ./load-images.sh --bundle rl-bundle-2026.tar.gz --registry my-registry.local
3) Apply CRDs and namespace manifests: kubectl apply -f manifests/crds.yaml
4) Install Helm chart configured for local registry and storage: helm install redwood --values values-offline.yaml redwood-chart.tgz
5) Verify readiness: ./scripts/check-health.sh --namespace redwood

4) Day-2 Operations (Runbooks)
Observability & alerting (core alerts):
- Control Plane Unhealthy: any control-plane replica Down for > 5 minutes.
- GPU Utilization Saturation: GPU utilization > 85% for 10 minutes.
- KV Cache Eviction Spike: evictions > baseline * 3 for 5 minutes.
Dashboards to maintain: per-model latency, per-route cost, token throughput, node GPU heatmap.

Backups & model store policy:
- Model artifacts (object store): daily snapshot with default 7-day retention (configurable).
- Control-plane metadata DB: nightly logical backups; recommend point-in-time recovery when using managed DBs.
- Quarterly test restores in a non-production environment.

Scaling & capacity best practices:
- Horizontal GPU scaling via autoscaler (trigger: CPU > 70% or GPU queue depth > 100 sustained for 3 minutes).
- Pre-warming: schedule cold-model preloads during off-peak windows for frequently used models.
- Capacity planning: maintain ~20% headroom above expected p95 throughput for production workloads.

Routine maintenance checklist:
- Daily: alert triage, control-plane health check, backup verification.
- Weekly: security updates review, disk usage, model registry integrity scans.
- Monthly: restore drill, dependency patching, capacity review with stakeholders.

5) Upgrade & Rollback Procedures
Principles:
- Always validate upgrades in a non-production environment first.
- Automate preflight checks and abort on failures.
- Use canary rollouts for control-plane and routing changes.

Preflight checks (automated):
- Cluster health: all nodes Ready, disk usage < 70%.
- Backup verification: successful backup in last 24 hours.
- Model compatibility: validate model schemas for any updated artifacts.
- Capture SLO baseline snapshot for last 24 hours (latency, error rate).

Canary upgrade (step-by-step example):
1) Bump chart version and set canary label to 10% of control-plane traffic via rollout controller.
2) Deploy new control-plane revision to a single canary replica: helm upgrade --set canary.enabled=true ...
3) Monitor metrics for 30-60 minutes (errors, latency, token throughput).
4) If stable, increase canary weight to 50% for 1 hour.
5) If stable, roll out to remaining replicas via rolling upgrade with maxUnavailable=1 and surge=1.

Automated rollback triggers (recommended thresholds):
- Error rate increase > 3x baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- Latency p95 increase > 40% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Resource exhaustion events (OOM, GPU driver failure).

Manual rollback procedure (short):
1) Pause rollout: kubectl rollout pause deploy/control-plane.
2) Roll back to previous revision: kubectl rollout undo deploy/control-plane --to-revision=<previous>.
3) Verify health: ./scripts/check-health.sh.
4) Open an incident and notify stakeholders per escalation matrix if customer impact is observed.

6) Customer Requirements Library (scoping checklist)
Note: Present this checklist during customer scoping meetings. Items marked Required must be provided prior to onboarding.

Minimum customer requirements (summary items):
- VPC connectivity: Minimum — dedicated private connectivity (VPN or Transit Gateway). Recommended — Direct Connect / ExpressRoute for <10ms steady latency.
- Image pulls: Minimum — temporary outbound internet access to Redwood registry OR provide offline bundle. Recommended — local registry with mirrored images for air-gapped installs.
- KMS / HSM: Minimum — ability to provide a customer key for at-rest encryption (optional). Recommended — customer-managed KMS integration with control-plane.
- GPU drivers & nodes: Minimum — GPUs with CUDA 11.x compatible drivers. Recommended — validated GPU instance types from our driver matrix (A100, A10G, T4).
- SLA & compliance: Minimum — defined availability objectives and maintenance windows. Recommended — penetration test and SOC2 evidence exchange for enterprise deployments.

Common customer pitfalls & mitigations:
- Pitfall: Insufficient registry mirror capacity in air-gapped installs. Mitigation: Provide preloaded registry images and verify via preflight.
- Pitfall: Time drift causing cert validation errors. Mitigation: Enforce NTP/time sync and include time-check in preflight.
- Pitfall: Network egress blocking image pulls during install. Mitigation: Provide offline bundle or temporary egress rules during onboarding.

7) Ownership and Escalation
- Owner: Eng Private Deployments (eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai).
- Oncall escalation path: Customer SRE -> Eng Private Deployments -> Runtime & Kernel Team -> CTO on call.
- Support windows: 24x7 for production under enterprise contracts; business-hours support for self-serve deployments.

8) Security & Compliance Notes
- Audit logging: enable granular audit logs for admin actions; default retention 90 days (configurable per customer).
- RBAC: enforce least privilege roles for deployers; read-only roles for auditors.
- Data residency: ensure model artifact storage location meets customer residency and retention policies.

9) Appendix A — Driver & Runtime Matrix (excerpt)
- CUDA 11.8: supported for A10G, T4.
- CUDA 11.6: legacy drivers (supported only for legacy clusters; not recommended).
- NVIDIA driver >= 515: required for A100 series.

10) Appendix B — Example values.yaml snippet (partial)
# Partial example; real deployments require customer-specific overrides
image:
  repository: my-registry.local/redwood/inference
  tag: 2026.02.0
controlPlane:
  replicas: 4
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "2000m"
      memory: "8Gi"
    limits:
      cpu: "4000m"
      memory: "16Gi"
